subject.title: Feature: Handle Signal message edits (editMessage envelope)

question: What Signal `editMessage` behavior should OpenClaw guarantee: transcript replacement, appended edit metadata, marker-only handling, or deferral to the broader cross-channel lifecycle contract?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the durable transcript, dedupe, and reply-trigger semantics affect user-visible session state and should not be chosen by cleanup automation alone.

options.title: Implement Signal-local edit semantics
options.body: Type `targetSentTimestamp`, carry edit metadata or an `[edited]` marker, update or dedupe against the original message according to a documented policy, and suppress non-mentioned group edit replies.

options.title: Defer to lifecycle umbrella
options.body: Keep this issue blocked until https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/55691 defines shared edit/delete/recall semantics across channels.

options.title: Accept marker-only scope
options.body: Only mark edited Signal messages while leaving transcript replacement, cancellation, and reply suppression for a later product decision.

recommendation.title: Implement Signal-local edit semantics
recommendation.body: Type `targetSentTimestamp`, carry edit metadata or an `[edited]` marker, update or dedupe against the original message according to a documented policy, and suppress non-mentioned group edit replies.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger has the strongest history on the Signal inbound and channel-routing code paths where the behavior would live.
